title: New reset-arm grep guard is not unique to the reset arm — also matches the pre-existing consent-opt-out branch
evidence:
Guard pin added in both chains:
Makefile:274: `           'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' \`
Dockerfile:133: `    && grep -q -F 'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' server/priv/static/index.html \`

That exact substring also occurs in the PRE-EXISTING consent-changed else arm (unchanged by this PR), read verbatim from Makefile:193 snippet:
`opt_out_capturing();document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;}});`

The changed reset arm itself (Makefile:193) reads:
`var k=rtPhOk();document.cookie="rt_ph_reset=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;window.posthog.reset();`
detail: Round context requires the guard pins be 'substrings UNIQUE to the changed arm.' This pin is satisfied by the pre-existing consent-opt-out branch too, so reverting only the reset-arm rt_landlord_id clear would still pass CI — the guard does not defend its stated regression.
recommended_fix: Pin a substring unique to the reset arm, e.g. `rt_ph_reset=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;window.posthog.reset()` (adjacent rt_ph_reset clear + reset() call disambiguate it), in both Makefile and Dockerfile guard lists.
